requirements.statement: For each layout table, the content read in linear order remains understandable: the order in which the cells are reached is consistent with the content.

citations.quote: Pour chaque tableau de mise en forme, le contenu linéarisé reste-t-il compréhensible ?

routes.statement: The order of access to the cells is consistent with the content.

citations.quote: L’ordre d’accès aux cellules est cohérent avec le contenu ;

requirements.statement: For each layout table, the table element has role="presentation".

citations.quote: Chaque tableau de mise en forme vérifie-t-il ces conditions ?

routes.statement: The table element carries the attribute role="presentation".

citations.quote: L’élément `<table>` est pourvu d’un attribut WAI-ARIA `role="presentation"`.

rationale.text: The wording asks each layout table to meet both conditions, so they are two requirements, each with one route. The first is judgment: whether the order of the cells is consistent with the content, and whether the linear content stays understandable, cannot be decided by code. The second is mechanical once a table is known to be a layout table, but that is the obstacle. The glossary defines a layout table by its purpose, controlling the display of information through cells, and a data table also uses the table element; a table without role="presentation" may be a data table, to which this test does not apply. So no table is surely in scope, and a fault on a table without the attribute could be a false failure. The entry is none and has no links: no axe rule is tagged for this test, and no deterministic check could prove its failure. The wording names only role="presentation"; role="none", its ARIA synonym, is not named, so a check built later must not count it as meeting the second requirement without an official text that says so. What would raise the second requirement to fail_only: a markup-based, official way to recognise a layout table. Applicability is judgment, for the same reason. Needs is empty: the order of the cells is read from the page as loaded.

citations.quote: Technique qui utilise un élément HTML (balise <table>) pour contrôler l’affichage d’informations via des cellules (balise <td>).
Un tableau de données est une structure introduite par une balise <table>
Retrouver dans le document les tableaux de mise en forme ;
Si c’est le cas pour chaque tableau de mise en forme, **le test est validé**.
